talwar.name: Talwar
talwar.subtitle: The Curved Killing Blade
talwar.description: The quintessential Rajput sword. Its curved blade is engineered for the draw-cut, capable of decapitating an enemy in a single fluid motion from horseback.

khanda.name: Khanda
khanda.subtitle: The Double-Edged Cleaver
khanda.description: A straight, heavy, double-edged sword with a reinforced spine. Designed to hack through mail and bone. A weapon of brute force and religious significance.

firangi.name: Firangi
firangi.subtitle: The Foreign Blade
firangi.description: Imported European blades (Portuguese/German) mounted on Hindu basket hilts. Used for their superior reach and thrusting capability in cavalry charges.

pata.name: Pata
pata.subtitle: The Gauntlet Sword
pata.description: A sword integrated into a steel gauntlet. The warrior becomes the weapon. Impossible to disarm, used for slashing through infantry lines.

saif.name: Saif
saif.subtitle: The Straight Edge
saif.description: A broad, straight-bladed sword of Arab origin adapted by Rajputs. Focuses on durability and piercing power against chainmail.

tulwar.name: Tulwar
tulwar.subtitle: Variant Curved Saber
tulwar.description: A heavier variation of the Talwar with a deeper curve, optimizing the mechanics of the draw cut for dismounted combat.

tegha.name: Tegha
tegha.subtitle: The Executioner's Blade
tegha.description: A massive, broad curved sword. Too heavy for prolonged combat, used for executions or by the strongest warriors to sever limbs in one blow.

asi.name: Asi
asi.subtitle: The Lotus Blade
asi.description: An ancient form of sword mentioned in epics, precursor to the Khanda. Represents the primordial sword created to destroy evil.

karavela.name: Karavela
karavela.subtitle: The Sickle Blade
karavela.description: A sword with a distinct sickle-like curve, designed to hook shields and limbs.

katar.name: Katar
katar.subtitle: The Punching Dagger
katar.description: The most famous Rajput dagger. An H-shaped handle allows the warrior to put their full body weight behind a thrust that can pierce armor.

bichuwa.name: Bichuwa
bichuwa.subtitle: The Scorpion
bichuwa.description: A double-curved dagger resembling a scorpion's sting. Often looped over fingers, used for concealed, upward gutting strikes.

chhuri.name: Chhuri
chhuri.subtitle: The War Knife
chhuri.description: A single-edged knife with a slightly curved blade. A utility tool that doubles as a deadly close-range weapon.

jamdhar.name: Jamdhar
jamdhar.subtitle: The Death Tooth
jamdhar.description: A broad-bladed variant of the Katar. "Jamdhar" implies the tooth of Yama, the God of Death. Inflicts massive, gaping wounds.

pesh-kabz.name: Pesh-kabz
pesh-kabz.subtitle: The Mail Piercer
pesh-kabz.description: A dagger with a T-spine designed specifically to split chainmail links. The tip is reinforced for maximum penetration.

khanjar.name: Khanjar
khanjar.subtitle: The Curved Fang
khanjar.description: A dagger with a recurved blade, often with a pistol-grip hilt. Optimized for slashing capability.

jambiya.name: Jambiya
jambiya.subtitle: The Arab Influence
jambiya.description: A curved dagger with a medial ridge. Adopted from Arab traders and mercenaries, integrated into Rajput armories.

bhala.name: Bhala
bhala.subtitle: The Infantry Spear
bhala.description: The standard spear of the Rajput foot soldier. A bamboo or wood shaft with a razor-sharp steel head.

barchha.name: Barchha
barchha.subtitle: The Heavy Lance
barchha.description: A heavy, all-metal lance used by cavalry. Could penetrate shields and armor through the sheer momentum of a charge.

ballam.name: Ballam
ballam.subtitle: The Short Spear
ballam.description: A shorter spear used for close-quarters skirmishing or thrown as a heavy javelin.

sang.name: Sang
sang.subtitle: The Iron Pike
sang.description: A long lance made entirely of iron. Used by heavy cavalry to break enemy formations. Often possessed a quadrangular tip.

kont.name: Kont
kont.subtitle: The Spiked Staff
kont.description: A spear with a long, faceted blade, often used to penetrate deep into targets.

trishul.name: Trishul
trishul.subtitle: The Trident
trishul.description: A three-pronged spear. While symbolic of Shiva, war variants were used to trap enemy weapons and disarm opponents.

halberd-rajput.name: Rajput Halberd
halberd-rajput.subtitle: The Axe-Spear
halberd-rajput.description: Indian variants of the halberd, combining a spear tip with an axe blade or hook. Versatile against both cavalry and infantry.

parashu.name: Parashu
parashu.subtitle: The Battle Axe
parashu.description: The classical Indian battle axe. Single or double-bladed, used to deliver crushing blows that ignore armor.

tabar.name: Tabar
tabar.subtitle: The Saddle Axe
tabar.description: A light battle axe often carried by cavalry in a saddle holster. Perfect for breaking helmets in a melee.

pharsa.name: Pharsa
pharsa.subtitle: The Heavy Cleaver
pharsa.description: A long-handled axe used by foot soldiers. Its reach allowed it to be brought down with tremendous force on shielded enemies.

gajdal.name: Gajdal
gajdal.subtitle: The Elephant Axe
gajdal.description: A massive axe designed to attack war elephants or be used by elephant riders.

double-axe.name: Double-Bladed Axe
double-axe.subtitle: The Whirling Death
double-axe.description: Rare double-headed axes used by elite shock troops for clearing space in a melee.

gada.name: Gada
gada.subtitle: The Mace
gada.description: A heavy spherical or flanged mace. A weapon of pure strength, used to shatter bones through armor.

gurz.name: Gurz
gurz.subtitle: The Flanged Mace
gurz.description: A mace with metal flanges (wings) designed to concentrate force and dent plate armor.

mudgar.name: Mudgar
mudgar.subtitle: The War Club
mudgar.description: A heavy wooden club, sometimes reinforced with iron. Used for strength training and brute combat.

spiked-mace.name: Spiked Mace
spiked-mace.subtitle: The Morning Star
spiked-mace.description: A mace head covered in spikes, adding puncture damage to blunt force impact.

war-hammer.name: War Hammer
war-hammer.subtitle: The Armor Breaker
war-hammer.description: A hammer with a pick on the reverse side. Designed to punch holes in helmets and breastplates.

dhanush.name: Dhanush
dhanush.subtitle: The Bamboo Bow
dhanush.description: The traditional self bow made of bamboo. Simple, reliable, and effective in massed volleys.

composite-bow.name: Rajput Composite Bow
composite-bow.subtitle: The Recurve
composite-bow.description: A complex bow of horn, wood, and sinew. High draw weight and compact size made it perfect for horse archers.

crossbow.name: Crossbow
crossbow.subtitle: The Mechanical Bolt
crossbow.description: Though less common, crossbows were used for siege defense and by specialized units for armor piercing.

chakram.name: Chakram
chakram.subtitle: The Flying Disc
chakram.description: A sharp steel quoit thrown with a spinning motion. Capable of severing necks and limbs at range.

sling.name: Sling
sling.subtitle: The Stone Thrower
sling.description: A simple weapon used to hurl stones or lead bullets with surprising force. Used by light infantry.

javelin.name: Javelin
javelin.subtitle: The Thrown Spear
javelin.description: Light spears balanced for throwing. Used to break up enemy charges before contact.

matchlock.name: Matchlock (Bandook)
matchlock.subtitle: The Fire Stick
matchlock.description: Early muzzle-loading muskets. Long barrels provided accuracy, used by snipers from fort walls.

jezail.name: Jezail
jezail.subtitle: The Long Rifle
jezail.description: A long-barreled musket with a curved stock. Famous for its range and accuracy in rough terrain.

toradar.name: Toradar
toradar.subtitle: The Matchlock Variant
toradar.description: An Indian matchlock musket. Characterized by a straight stock and often held against the cheek.

flintlock.name: Flintlock Musket
flintlock.subtitle: The Spark Lock
flintlock.description: Adopted later, replacing the matchlock. Provided faster reloading and reliability in wet weather.

hand-cannon.name: Hand Cannon
hand-cannon.subtitle: The Thunder Tube
hand-cannon.description: Primitive portable firearms. Essentially a small tube on a stick, firing stones or metal scrap.

swivel-gun.name: Swivel Gun
swivel-gun.subtitle: The Wall Gun
swivel-gun.description: Large caliber guns mounted on walls or camels (Zamburak). Bridged the gap between musket and cannon.

rajput-cannon.name: Rajput Cannon
rajput-cannon.subtitle: The Fort Breaker
rajput-cannon.description: Massive bronze or iron cannons cast in local foundries. Essential for fort defense and siege warfare.

zamburak.name: Zamburak
zamburak.subtitle: The Camel Cannon
zamburak.description: A light swivel cannon mounted on a saddle on a camel. Allowed for mobile artillery tactics in the desert.

elephant-gun.name: Elephant Gun
elephant-gun.subtitle: The Howdah Cannon
elephant-gun.description: Small cannons or jingals mounted on elephant howdahs, providing high-angle fire over infantry lines.

rocket.name: War Rocket
rocket.subtitle: The Fire Arrow
rocket.description: Bamboo or metal tubes filled with gunpowder and attached to a long stabilizing stick. Early area-denial weapon.

battering-ram.name: Battering Ram
battering-ram.subtitle: The Gate Breaker
battering-ram.description: A massive log, often tipped with iron, swung to breach heavy fort gates.

siege-tower.name: Siege Tower
siege-tower.subtitle: The Moving Fort
siege-tower.description: Wooden towers rolled up to enemy walls to allow troops to storm the ramparts.

catapult.name: Catapult
catapult.subtitle: The Stone Thrower
catapult.description: Tension-powered siege engines used to hurl stones at walls or over them.

fire-pot.name: Fire Pot
fire-pot.subtitle: The Incendiary
fire-pot.description: Clay pots filled with combustibles, thrown to start fires or burn enemy siege engines.

boiling-oil.name: Boiling Oil
boiling-oil.subtitle: The Wall Defense
boiling-oil.description: Cauldrons of boiling oil or molten lead poured through murder holes onto attackers.

dhal.name: Dhal
dhal.subtitle: The Shield
dhal.description: Convex circular shield of hide or steel. Four bosses serve as anchor points for the handle and catch blades.

sipar.name: Sipar
sipar.subtitle: The Steel Shield
sipar.description: A steel shield, often intricately decorated. Heavier than hide shields but offered superior protection against muskets.

katar-shield.name: Katar Shield
katar-shield.subtitle: The Weaponized Shield
katar-shield.description: A small buckler with two projecting blades, often used in conjunction with a dagger.

chainmail.name: Zirh (Chainmail)
chainmail.subtitle: The Steel Mesh
chainmail.description: Interlinked steel rings worn as a shirt. Flexible protection against cuts, though vulnerable to piercing.

plate-armor.name: Plate Armor (Chilta)
plate-armor.subtitle: The Iron Skin
plate-armor.description: Rigid steel plates, often combined with mail (plated mail), offering maximum protection for heavy cavalry.

helmet.name: Kulah-khud
helmet.subtitle: The Steel Bowl
helmet.description: Bowl-shaped helmet with a nose guard and chainmail aventail to protect the neck.

lance-cavalry.name: Cavalry Lance
lance-cavalry.subtitle: The Charge Weapon
lance-cavalry.description: Long bamboo or steel lance used for the initial shock charge.

stirrups.name: War Stirrups
stirrups.subtitle: The Foundation
stirrups.description: Heavy iron stirrups allowed a rider to stand and deliver powerful blows without losing balance.

saddle-blade.name: Saddle Blade
saddle-blade.subtitle: The Horse's Fang
saddle-blade.description: Blades attached to the saddle to cut enemy infantry who get too close.

horse-armor.name: Bakhter (Horse Armor)
horse-armor.subtitle: The Mount's Shield
horse-armor.description: Lamellar or mail armor for war horses, protecting them from arrows and sword cuts.

war-banner.name: War Banner
war-banner.subtitle: The Rally Point
war-banner.description: Symbols of the clan or deity. Protecting the banner was a matter of honor; losing it signaled defeat.

war-horse.name: Marwari War Horse
war-horse.subtitle: The Desert Steed
war-horse.description: Indigenous breed known for inward-turning ear tips and incredible endurance. Bred for battle.

war-elephant.name: War Elephant
war-elephant.subtitle: The Living Tank
war-elephant.description: Armored elephants used to trample infantry and smash gates. The ultimate shock weapon.

tusk-blade.name: Tusk Blades
tusk-blade.subtitle: The Ivory Swords
tusk-blade.description: Swords attached to elephant tusks. Turned a head swipe into a multi-kill scythe.

elephant-tower.name: Howdah
elephant-tower.subtitle: The Mobile Fort
elephant-tower.description: A fortified seat on an elephant, carrying archers or commanders above the melee.

shakti.name: Shakti
shakti.subtitle: The Divine Spear
shakti.description: A ritual spear associated with Goddess Durga. Worshipped during weapon consecration ceremonies.

sacred-sword.name: Sacred Sword
sacred-sword.subtitle: The Ancestral Blade
sacred-sword.description: Swords passed down for generations, believed to hold the spirit of ancestors. Rarely used in battle.

victory-standard.name: Vijay Stambh
victory-standard.subtitle: The Victory Pillar
victory-standard.description: While not a handheld weapon, these monuments were the ultimate declaration of martial dominance.

temple-weapon.name: Temple Weapon
temple-weapon.subtitle: The Blessed Arm
temple-weapon.description: Weapons kept in temples, blessed by priests, and brought out only for defense of the faith.

coronation-blade.name: Raj Tilak Sword
coronation-blade.subtitle: The Kingmaker
coronation-blade.description: The sword used during the coronation ceremony. To touch it is to accept the burden of ruling.
